depicted_variant: An original menacing tree yōkai bending seizing branches toward viewer on abandoned battlefield.

visual_requirements.description: Tree-like yokai, branches capable of seizing people; no invented face or walking legs

aura: Physical seizing branch action c03 makes tree c01 the active creature; no aura or anthropomorphic face.
artistic_choices: Entirely original tree form, no reproduction of Saito/Mizuki manga design.
No blood, victims or wounds; grasping branch movement stages documented capability before contact.
Old blank broken spear shafts half-buried in ground are editorial battlefield cue; no text or insignia.
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Jubokko, the tree-like yokai of modern Japanese stories haunting former battlefields. Entirely original design, do not copy any manga or anime tree character.
ANATOMY: ONE huge living GNARLED TREE with thick rooted trunk and many crooked BRANCHES, rough black-brown bark; NO human face, eyes, mouth, hands, legs or anthropomorphic body invented. Branch tips remain wooden branching twigs, not fingers [jubokko-c01,jubokko-c03].
MOMENT: Bend the whole trunk down toward viewer while THREE main crooked branches reach forcefully in from above and both sides, curling around the near foreground as if about to seize; roots tear soil and small stones upward through PHYSICAL motion. No person or victim in scene.
POWER: branches physically seize approaching people in story; depict imminent grasping action without contact, blood, wounds, dead bodies or feeding. No magic rays or aura [jubokko-c03].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low near-root close angle; knotty trunk and grasping wooden branches dominate square, viewer trapped in their converging shapes; not a distant landscape.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one amber moon shaft catches bark edges and dust, deep warm walnut shadows; ordinary windblown dead leaves and soil.
SURFACE: coarse split ancient bark, moss, splintered twig tips, disturbed soil.
SETTING: abandoned former Japanese battlefield, a few blank broken spear shafts half-buried under old grass as secondary editorial cue, no symbols [jubokko-c02].
MOOD: active overwhelming danger from a moving predatory tree, never ordinary static tree, calm landscape or cute face-tree.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Jubokko
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one original tree yokai with forcefully curved grasping branches converging on viewer, bent trunk and uplifted soil/roots, no human face/limbs invented. Subject dominates tight low angle and remains threatening at 200px, not a landscape. Bare abandoned battlefield markers secondary. No copied character, victims, gore, text or aura. All seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px + 200px + trunk and background crops. A single huge gnarled tree is the whole subject (jubokko-c07/c02): a twisted mossy trunk and bark with no anthropomorphic face (the trunk crop confirms only bark texture) and no legs. Its branches bend and reach toward the viewer like splintered grasping claws — the blood-draining tree that seizes passers-by (jubokko-c03) — rendered without any victim or blood. Set on a moonlit former battlefield with broken weapon shafts standing in the dead ground (jubokko-c02). An original realistic depiction, NOT Shigeru Mizuki's cartoon design (jubokko-c04/c05/c06); no text, no aura. The twisted menacing tree dominates at 200px, not an empty landscape.
